name: Pediatric clinics (category guide)
summary: Private paediatricians vs polyclinic vaccines for foreign kids — cash fees, NIR catch-up, and when KKH/NUH beats a mall clinic after hours.
body: EP/DP children pay unsubsidised rates at polyclinics and public hospitals — ‘public equals cheap’ is a citizen myth. Routine National Childhood Immunisation Schedule catch-up often still runs through polyclinics for NIR recording even when you keep a private paediatrician for fever and travel consults. Private paediatric clinics (islandwide chains and boutique practices) win on continuity and English-first access; cash/card consults commonly sit well above GP rates, and after-hours fees spike. For true emergencies, know KKH or NUH children’s A&E — Thomson-style 24-hour kids clinics help for urgent-but-not-critical nights. Ask HR whether your group plan panels named paediatric clinics and what outpatient caps look like; many riders treat kids’ consults like adult GP visits with low annual ceilings. Bring overseas vaccine cards to the first visit; undocumented doses get repeated. This is a category guide, not a ranked paediatrician list — verify panels, NIR uploads, and cash fee sheets yourself.
